observation_summary: The Closure Compiler emits an incorrect warning ('@this type of a function must be an object') when a typedef is used in a @this annotation, even though the typedef resolves to a valid object type. This regression prevents valid code from compiling without warnings.
hypothesis: The type inference engine fails to correctly resolve typedefs when they are used in @this annotations. It treats the resolved type as a primitive or non-object type, triggering a validation check that expects an object type for @this, whereas it should correctly identify the underlying object structure of the typedef.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the type resolution logic (likely in the type inference or JSDoc processing component) to correctly unwrap or resolve the typedef to its underlying object type before validating the @this annotation.
experiment_rationale: The failure occurs during type checking when the compiler encounters a @this annotation referencing a typedef. The error message indicates the compiler sees the type as something other than an object (e.g., 'Actual type: (Array|null|undefined)'), suggesting the resolution mechanism is failing to recognize the typedef as a valid object type.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the type inference/resolution procedure. The compiler incorrectly identifies the type of a typedef as invalid for a @this context. This is a procedural logic error in how the compiler processes type annotations, not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple value assignment error. It is an algorithmic failure in the type system's resolution logic.
evidence_used: The error message 'JSC_THIS_TYPE_NON_OBJECT. @this type of a function must be an object' occurs when using a typedef in @this.
The test cases 'testBackwardsTypedefUse8' and 'testBackwardsTypedefUse9' demonstrate that valid typedefs are being rejected.
The bug report confirms that '@this {bug.A|bug.B} works' but '@this {bug.Thing}' (where Thing is a typedef) fails, indicating the resolution of the typedef is the root cause.
evidence_gaps: The specific file containing the type resolution logic is not provided in the snippets, but the behavior is clearly localized to the type inference/checking pass.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the error is triggered by a check, the root cause is that the type system incorrectly resolves the typedef, making the check fail on valid input. The logic error is in the resolution algorithm, not the check itself.
This is not a missing capability or design-level omission; it is a regression in existing type resolution logic.
